Issue 115's superseded E30 wording ('legal privileges to use material and immaterial things and their derivatives') is also verified verbatim.

decisive_difference: B is held back by a genuine modelling gap rather than a style difference: the case asks in as many words whether the retention schedule belongs in documented history, and B never types the schedule (no E29), while also reaching for a less specific class (E13, not E17) where the more specific one fits the scope note better, and leaning on a t1306 quote whose own message concludes the opposite of what B uses it to argue. Between A and C, both are legal, scope-note-consistent and well-cited; C edges ahead by covering the case's literal destruction outcome (E6) with a properly caveated class, by adding a verified Monotonicity argument A doesn't use, and by carrying the CRMsoc/CRMact history one step further (Issue 419's move out of CRMsoc, Issue 557's discontinuation) plus an exact, highly on-point 2005 precedent (Scheduled Treatment) that neither A nor B located. A is nearly as strong and deliberately, transparently excludes E6 as out of scope for the specific question asked, which is defensible rather than wrong.
